hook.text: Russian has two mandatory words for blue—'siniy' (dark blue) and 'goluboy' (light blue).

buildup.text: Languages divide the color spectrum differently—some have only two or three basic color terms.

discovery.text: Berlin and Kay found a universal hierarchy: if a language has three terms, they're black, white, and red.

twist.text: Russian speakers distinguish blues faster than English speakers—language affects perception.

climax.text: Color naming sits at the intersection of biology, culture, and language.

punchline.text: The colors you name are the colors you see faster.

quiz.question: What did Berlin and Kay discover about color terms?
options: All languages have the same number
